answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil swarms by tying voting weight to an aged anchor stake. Each new agent locks a bond that sits in a quiet meadow period for several epochs, earning no say while peers watch its behavior. Only after that wait does the anchor convert into influence, and an opal-style audit, a random sample of the agent's past outputs graded by unrelated reviewers, must pass first. Clones that copy each other fail the audit together and lose their bonds, so faking many identities means funding many locked stakes and waiting out every meadow.
